observations: Photo 0: A removed car engine block with black plastic engine cover, attached front subframe, and two coilover strut/spring assemblies, sitting on wet pavement.

Photo 1: Same or similar engine pulled further back, showing a transmission bolted to the engine, exhaust manifolds/catalytic converters, and axle/CV joint boots, surrounded by other scrap engines in a yard.
Photo 2: Overhead view of the engine with transmission, red-painted brackets, coil struts on both sides, and visible dirt/oil residue on the engine cover.
A watermark reading 'EZE PORSCHE GLOBAL AUTOS' appears across all three photos; this is the seller's business name, not a readable brand/model on the part itself.
No manufacturer logo, part number, or engine code is legible on the block, cover, or transmission casing in any photo.
All items appear to be used, pulled from a vehicle, with visible dirt, grease, and surface corrosion on bolts and brackets.

identity.kind: used car engine with transmission and front suspension struts (complete engine pull-out assembly)

claims.claim: We also deals on all kinds of car spare parts
claims.evidence: General business statement, not tied to any specific photo; no catalog or storefront shown.

risks.risk: Engine may not run, start, or have compression; no video or sound evidence of operation.
risks.proof: A video clip of the engine being started/running, or a compression test reading.
risks.if_unproven: priced as non-running, for parts/rebuild only

risks.risk: Transmission condition unknown (gear engagement, fluid leaks, internal wear).
risks.proof: Video of transmission shifting through gears when connected, or fluid level/color check.

risks.risk: Mismatched components: engine, transmission, and struts could be from different donor vehicles, creating compatibility issues.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of matching VIN/engine code stickers or casting numbers on engine, transmission, and struts.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unverified compatibility, buyer assumes integration risk

risks.risk: Hidden cracks, weld repairs, or corrosion under dirt/grime on block or subframe.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of cleaned block surface, oil pan, and subframe welds.
risks.if_unproven: priced as cosmetic/structural condition unverified, worst case assumed

risks.risk: Missing ancillary parts (sensors, wiring harness, starter, alternator) not visible or confirmed present.
risks.proof: Full inventory photo list of included components with harness and sensors visible.
risks.if_unproven: priced as bare long block only, accessories excluded

risks.risk: No identifiable engine code/model confirmed, so correct vehicle fitment cannot be verified.
risks.proof: Photo of engine code stamp/plate or casting number location.
risks.if_unproven: priced generically as unidentified used engine assembly, lower end of range

proof_requests: Close-up photo of engine code/casting number stamped on the block.
Video of the engine being started or turned over, with sound.
Wider shot showing all included parts (harness, sensors, mounts) laid out together.
Close-up of any welds, cracks, or repairs on the block and subframe.
response.reason: The photos clearly show a used, unidentified-brand car engine pulled with its transmission and front struts, but no running condition, compatibility, or completeness can be confirmed, so it is priced at worst case as a non-verified, non-running parts assembly.
